text:
nick_cust: Hey team, after we migrated our service behind PrivateLink we're seeing a bunch of TLS handshake failures from clients. API returns 502/empty body intermittently. Can you help?

maria_support: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the curl output and the DNS resolution from inside your VPC? Also which type of endpoint did you create (Interface endpoint -> NLB backed)?

nick_cust: created interface endpoint -> NLB -> target group (IP) -> our ALB. dns resolves to the vpce DNS name and to a private IP. curl to the vpce DNS yields: 
```
curl -v https://api.internal.example.com
* Connected to vpce-abc-123.vpce-svc-xxxx.amazonaws.com (10.10.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLS handshake failed: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
* Closing connection 0
```

Also tried `openssl s_client -connect 10.10.5.12:443 -servername api.internal.example.com` and the server returns the ALB certificate (common name = my-alb-123.us-west-2.elb.amazonaws.com).

maria_support: that last bit is suspicious. PrivateLink -> NLB is L4 so it forwards bytes to targets. If your target is an ALB and the ALB terminates TLS with its own cert (alb hostname), SNI will matter. Did you configure the NLB to forward raw TLS to the ALB? Usually NLB -> ALB combination is not supported for PrivateLink because ALB expects host header/SNI for the cert matching.

sophie_infra: yep — mixing a PrivateLink NLB with an ALB behind it commonly causes SNI/certificate mismatch and health check routing issues. ALB emits its own cert (alb hostname) so client sees wrong cert for api.internal.example.com. Two quick checks: 1) are your target group health checks passing? 2) what are your NLB listeners (TLS passthrough vs TLS termination)?

nick_cust: health checks show 3/3 but sometimes they flip to 0/3 for a few seconds. Listener is TCP:443 on NLB (no cert attached). Targets are the ALB IPs.

aj_solutions: follow-up: if NLB is TCP and targets are ALB IPs, the ALB will see the original client IP but ALB won't be able to select the correct certificate unless SNI is preserved with the hostname the client used. For clients that use the vpce DNS name (vpce-xxx.vpce-svc-yyy.amazonaws.com) SNI will be the vpce name, not your api.internal.example.com, unless you use `--resolve` or rename. That explains the cert mismatch.

maria_support: workarounds: 1) terminate TLS at the NLB (TLS listener with cert for api.internal.example.com) and forward plain HTTP to ALB — but NLB must have the cert (Network Load Balancer TLS listener supports TLS termination only on NLBs with TLS listener config + ACM cert on NLB), or 2) move to using NLB -> your service instances (not ALB) so target certs match, or 3) use PrivateLink service backed by NLB directly to your service not via ALB.

nick_cust: we relied on ALB features (host-based routing + WAF). Moving away would be a lot of work. Can we instead map the vpce DNS to the ALB host via SNI rewrite?

sophie_infra: you can't rewrite SNI in-flight with AWS PrivateLink. SNI comes from client TLS ClientHello; NLB doesn't rewrite TLS SNI in TCP mode. You can do this if you terminate at NLB and re-initiate TLS to ALB using correct SNI, but that requires cert on NLB and double-TLS which is messy and might break WAF.

aj_solutions: other practical option: create a private hosted zone in the customer's VPC to point api.internal.example.com to the ALB private IPs directly (split-horizon DNS). But that only works if ALB exposes private IPs and routing/security allows it — and it bypasses PrivateLink security boundaries. Consider security implications.

maria_support: also check security groups and egress: ensure the interface endpoint's ENIs can talk to the ALB targets on the expected ports. Common pitfall: SG on ALB or targets denies traffic from the endpoint ENIs. Show us your SG inbound for port 443 and the endpoint ENI IPs.

nick_cust: SG inbound is `Allowed: 10.0.0.0/16:443` (our VPC). Endpoint ENIs are in 10.10.5.0/24 so should be covered. Here's a quick tcpdump from a bastion hitting the vpce IP: 
```
12:34:01 IP 10.0.1.12.52000 > 10.10.5.12.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240
12:34:01 IP 10.10.5.12.443 > 10.0.1.12.52000: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0
```
R as immediate reset occasionally.

sophie_infra: R means target (ALB or target) is rejecting sessions — could be that ALB is seeing Host/SNI mismatch and resetting. Check ALB access logs for the actual TLS SNI/Host it received. Also confirm NLB's target health check path — if it uses HTTP path, but NLB is TCP listener, health check must be TCP-level or use target group type health check appropriately.

nick_cust: ALB logs show requests arriving with Host header `vpce-abc-123.vpce-svc-xxxx.amazonaws.com`. So yes SNI/Host mismatch. Makes sense.

maria_support: ok next steps (assigning): 
- @sophie_infra to validate whether we can attach the cert to the NLB TLS listener in their account (quick test) and see if double-terminating TLS is feasible.
- @aj_solutions to draft a safe migration path (NLB directly to service vs Private DNS override vs re-architect for ALB features).
- @nick_cust: if ok, please collect ALB access logs for a 1-hour window and share with us, and confirm whether WAF rules are required by compliance (because terminating at NLB may bypass WAF).

deploy-bot: [automated] Observability: detected 18 TLS handshake failures from vpce-abc-123 between 18:02-18:12 UTC.

sophie_infra: quick command to reproduce from inside VPC (use the vpce private IP):
```
# force SNI to your hostname
openssl s_client -connect 10.10.5.12:443 -servername api.internal.example.com
```
If that returns the correct cert, NLB isn't the issue. If you still get ALB cert, then NLB->ALB path is rewriting/using vpce name upstream.

aj_solutions: I'll sketch the migration doc today and include a minimal PoC: spin up a small nginx behind NLB with cert for api.internal.example.com and point PrivateLink to it to prove TLS termination at NLB works.

maria_support: thanks all. Nick — keeping this escalated; we'll ping once PoC results are in. :thumbsup:

nick_cust: thanks, looked through options. I'll collect logs and confirm WAF constraints. Appreciate the help. :relieved:
